content.text:
I fixed it in `lib/adapters/http.js`. When a request times out, Node's http adapter now uses `config.timeoutErrorMessage` if one is set. Otherwise it still says `timeout of <n>ms exceeded`. The error code (`ECONNABORTED`, or `ETIMEDOUT` with `clarifyTimeoutError`) hasn't changed.

**Checked:** I ran a small script against a local server that never responds. With `timeoutErrorMessage: 'Custom'` the error message was `Custom` with code `ECONNABORTED`. Without it, the message was `timeout of 200ms exceeded`.

**Test results:** `test/unit/adapters/http.js` now has 57 passing and 2 failing.
- **"should respect the timeoutErrorMessage property"** now fails. Despite its name, this existing test expects the default text `timeout of 250ms exceeded` even when a custom message is set, so it was written against the bug. I left it alone as instructed; it needs updating to expect `'oops, timeout'`.
- **"should support max content length"** failed in one run with my change and didn't fail on the unchanged code. I didn't look into it. It's in an unrelated code path, so it's probably flaky, but I haven't confirmed that.
